verdicts.note: S2 (campaign home page headline 'A New Generation of Leadership') and S5 (forum: 'new ideas and a new generation of leadership') are two explicit statements of a renewal pitch, so high confidence holds. +1 rather than +2 fits: he is a first-time candidate but runs on state-government ties and the outgoing auditor's endorsement (S1, S4).

Campaign title 'The Experienced Choice' (S2), 12 years on the city council chairing finance and public safety (S1, S5), and a forum answer resting on that record (S5). Explicit and repeated, so high holds. -1 rather than -2 is right because he has never held this office or worked in an auditor's office.

notes: Considered and rejected spending for both candidates. Hulst's 'safeguard taxpayer resources' and his call for regular sub-agency audits (S2, S3, S5) are oversight language, but Harrison-Smith also backs auditing the sub-agencies and modernizing financial systems (S1, S5). Both describe running the office, not a position on county spending, so scoring one of them on spending would invent a difference. Reform: Hulst runs as an independent 'above partisanship' (S2, S3), but nothing in the dossier addresses money in politics or structural reform. No taxes, housing, safety or climate evidence for either candidate.
